title: How many line segments does each shape have?
description: The line segments in each shape of the speed bump sequence are counted and give three, twelve, forty eight, one hundred ninety two and seven hundred sixty eight. Each segment becomes four, so the counts are three times the powers of four.
teaching_notes: One idea: every segment is replaced by four segments, so the count is multiplied by four at each step. Watch for students who add four instead of multiplying by four.

source: Figure it Out Q5 (Try This), p.12
video_script.why: The child counts the line segments of each shape in the speed bump sequence by seeing what one step does to the count, using the method of the solved example where each new part adds a fixed number.
video_script.substitution: Each step multiplies the count by four, in place of adding two sticks for each new triangle.
video_script.anchor: the first shapes of the speed bump sequence with the segments counted under each
video_script.payoff_line: The segments are three times the powers of four

final_answer.value: 3, 12, 48, 192, 768, ... which is 3 times the powers of 4
final_answer.spoken: three times the powers of four

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, do the same again for each new shape. Twelve times four is forty eight.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Forty eight times four is one hundred ninety two. One hundred ninety two times four is seven hundred sixty eight.

<bookmark mark='more'/>Each new shape multiplies by four once more.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the third shape: 3 x 4 x 4 = 3 x 16 = 48, and 12 x 4 = 48

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the third shape. Three times four times four is three times sixteen, which is forty eight, and it matches.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3, 12, 48, 192, 768, ... which is 3 times the powers of 4

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The segments are three times the powers of four. <bookmark mark='why'/>They are three, twelve, forty eight, one hundred ninety two and seven hundred sixty eight. Each shape has four times as many as the one before.
